text:
sarah.support: FYI multiple customers reporting 502/504s for hosted inference endpoints since ~09:10 UTC. One sample:

Sarah (customer) pasted response: 
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"text-3b","prompt":"hi"}'
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-request-id: req_01F7X... 
< content-type: application/json

{"error":"upstream handshake timeout (tls)"}

mike.eng: looking at edge logs now. spike in TLS handshake timeouts from edge -> origin around 09:09-09:12 UTC in us-west-2. sample gateway trace: `EDGE->ORIGIN handshake timeout (no server_hello)` :eyes:

lena.sre: can you paste the request_id and origin? I'll run openssl/tcpdump. Also did we finish cert rotation last night? I recall a rotation at ~08:55 UTC.

sarah.support: req_01F7X..., origin node: origin-prod-usw2-12

mike.eng: quick DNS checks from my laptop:
`dig +short @8.8.8.8 api-origin-usw2.redwood.internal` -> (intermittent) SERVFAIL
`dig +short @1.1.1.1 api-origin-usw2.redwood.internal` -> 10.12.34.56

lena.sre: tcpdump shows SYN, SYN-ACK then connection teardown. openssl s_client -servername api-origin-usw2.redwood.internal -connect 10.12.34.56:443 shows:
"CONNECTED(00000003)"
"139865...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:???"

lena.sre: other hosts resolving to different IPs. suspect DNS propagation + low TTL combined with cert rotation created SNI mismatch: clients resolving to old LB IPs that don't serve the new chain.

tony.platform: we rotated intermediate chain 08:55 UTC (deploy lb-2026-03-17-v2). Canary passed but looks like some resolver paths cached older A records or negative-cached SERVFAILs. If client gets old IP but sends SNI for new hostname we can see handshake failures.

maria.support: several customers behind corp proxies reported the spike. Many corp resolvers negative-cache SERVFAILs for a long time which prolongs impact. They also often do stale DNS caching.

eng-infra-bot: deploy lb-2026-03-17-v2 completed at 08:55 UTC (deploy/3456). No automatic rollback.

mike.eng: immediate mitigations we should try:
- keep old cert chain present on legacy LB IPs (serve both chains)
- increase DNS TTL for lb selector to 300s to reduce flapping
- route traffic away from nodes returning stale IPs via routing policy (if feasible)

lena.sre: quick repro steps for oncall:
1) `dig +trace api-origin-usw2.redwood.internal` from affected region and from 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1
2) `openssl s_client -servername api-origin-usw2.redwood.internal -connect <ip>:443 -tlsextdebug -state` against IPs returned
3) correlate edge logs for "handshake timeout" and resolver IPs

eng-oncall: opening incident INC-2026-032-08. Marking P1 until mitigations in place. Assigning to eng-infra + platform.

tony.platform: I'll push config to accept both cert chains across LB pool and prepare a fast rollback of lb-2026-03-17-v2 if needed. If old cert is still valid we can re-add it to nodes quickly.

sarah.support: I'll notify affected customers with ETA ~30-45m and include these workarounds: retries with backoff, and note that corp proxies may be slower to recover.

mike.eng: follow-ups after mitigation:
- audit cert rotation rollback safety (ensure we can serve both chains)
- increase DNS health checks and monitor resolver error rates
- add resolver diversity in smart routing to avoid single-resolver dependency

sarah.support: thanks all. I'll keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
